title: Regularization in Machine Learning: L1, L2, and Elastic Net
description: An explanation to regularization and its main types: L1 (Lasso), L2 (Ridge), and Elastic Net.
content:
**Regularization** is a technique that helps to prevent model overfitting. It involves adding a penalty term to the model's loss function, which penalizes large parameter values, thereby discouraging complex models that may memorize noise and fluctuations within the dataset. Regularization helps to simplify the model and improve its generalization performance.

The three classic types of regularization are:
• L1-regularization (Lasso)
• L2-regularization (Ridge)
• Elastic Net

L1-regularization, also known as **Lasso**, adds the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients (weights) to the loss function multiplied by a hyperparameter controlling the strength of the penalty.

Key properties of L1-regularization:
• It pushes many coefficients exactly to zero, effectively performing feature selection.
• It enables interpretability, as a sparser model with fewer non-zero weights is easier to interpret.
• The absolute value function is not differentiable at zero, which means the loss function is not smooth mathematically and gradient descent is not applicable here.

L2-regularization, also known as **Ridge**, introduces a penalty equal to the sum of squared coefficients multiplied by a hyperparameter controlling the strength of the penalty.

Key properties of L2-regularization:
• It rarely drives coefficients to zero; instead, it distributes the penalty across all parameters and performs weight shrinkage.
• It is effective in multicollinearity scenarios, as it tends to spread the weight among correlated features rather than singling one out.
• The L2-penalty is smooth and differentiable everywhere, which is beneficial for general optimization techniques such as gradient descent.

**Elastic Net** regularization combines both L1- and L2-regularization penalty terms and represents a weighted linear combination of them.

Key properties of Elastic Net:
• It inherits the feature selection properties of L1-regularization.
• It inherits the multicollinearity-handling properties of L2-regularization.

Quick comparison:
• L1 (Lasso) - sparse weights, built-in feature selection, non-smooth at zero.
• L2 (Ridge) - shrunk weights, handles multicollinearity, smooth and differentiable.
• Elastic Net - a weighted mix of both: feature selection plus multicollinearity robustness.
